identification.summary: PurpleHaze is an activity cluster named by SentinelLABS, which assesses with high confidence that it is China-nexus [S2][S4]. SentinelLABS describes it as having loose ties to APT15, and says some PurpleHaze intrusions loosely overlap with UNC5174 [S2][S3]. SentinelLABS says it observed and countered an October 2024 reconnaissance operation against SentinelOne's own internet-facing servers [S4]. SentinelOne says the actors were unsuccessful and SentinelOne was not compromised [S1][S4].
identification.firstObserved: SentinelLABS reporting covers PurpleHaze and related ShadowPad intrusions from roughly July 2024 to March 2025; a September 2024 European media intrusion and October 2024 activity against a South Asian government-supporting entity and SentinelOne are the earliest dated PurpleHaze items found [S2][S3][S4].
identification.notes: PurpleHaze is a vendor-defined activity cluster, not a Microsoft-named actor, and no Microsoft name was found. SentinelLABS treats the PurpleHaze and ShadowPad clusters as multiple partially related intrusions, not one actor [S1][S4]. APT15 and UNC5174 are separate clusters named by other vendors; the overlaps are loose and should not be merged [S2][S3]. Press coverage lists APT15 aliases (Flea, Nylon Typhoon, Playful Taurus, Royal APT, Vixen Panda) [S2]; these are APT15 aliases, not PurpleHaze aliases.

attribution.confidence: SentinelLABS assesses with high confidence that PurpleHaze and the wider ShadowPad activity are China-nexus [S2][S4]. SentinelLABS describes the APT15 and UNC5174 links as loose or speculative, and says investigations continue [S1][S2].
attribution.basis: SentinelLABS cites overlaps in tooling and infrastructure: a Go-based reverse-shell backdoor (GoReShell), use of an operational relay box (ORB) network, and shared use of The Hacker's Choice (THC) tools [S2][S3]. ScatterBrain-obfuscated ShadowPad samples are tied by Google Threat Intelligence Group to APT41-associated clusters, which is a different attribution path from the APT15 overlap [S1]. No government attribution was found in the sources gathered.

sectors: IT hardware logistics provider serving SentinelOne employees [S1][S4]
Several other sectors (more than 70 ShadowPad-related organizations) [S2][S4]
regions: Global (ShadowPad victim set; regions not itemized in sources gathered) [S2]
targeting.notes: The 70-plus victim figure is for the broader ShadowPad activity, not PurpleHaze alone [S2][S4]. The Register is quoted as saying the researchers believe a count of 75 may be at the lower end of actual activity [S4]. SentinelOne reports it was not itself compromised [S1][S4].

capabilities.summary: SentinelLABS reports PurpleHaze use of an ORB network and GoReShell, a Go-based reverse-shell backdoor that connects over SSH [S2][S3]. The cluster shares use of The Hacker's Choice (THC) tools, which SentinelOne described as the first time state-sponsored actors were seen abusing THC software [S2][S3]. The broader ShadowPad intrusions used samples obfuscated with the ScatterBrain compiler [S2][S4]. SentinelLABS reported that ShadowPad was likely deployed after exploitation of an N-day flaw in Check Point gateway devices [S2]. Press coverage later said GOREVERSE, a GoReShell variant, appeared in SAP NetWeaver exploitation linked to UNC5174, which is a separate cluster [S3].

campaigns.name: ShadowPad intrusion at South Asian government-supporting entity
campaigns.summary: Earlier activity against the same entity later hit in October 2024; SentinelLABS did not confirm a link to PurpleHaze [S2].

campaigns.name: European media organization intrusion
campaigns.summary: GoReShell was linked to a September 2024 attack on a leading European media organization [S2].

campaigns.name: Reconnaissance against SentinelOne and South Asian government entity
campaigns.summary: SentinelLABS saw repeated attempts to open remote connections to internet-facing SentinelOne servers over port 443. In the same month the South Asian government-supporting entity was targeted using an ORB network and GoReShell [S1][S2][S4].

campaigns.name: Broader ShadowPad activity (more than 70 organizations)
campaigns.summary: SentinelLABS describes ShadowPad intrusions across several sectors in this period, with ScatterBrain-obfuscated samples [S2][S4].

campaigns.name: Intrusion at SentinelOne hardware logistics provider
campaigns.summary: Coverage places the breach of a third-party IT logistics provider for SentinelOne employee hardware in early 2025; one write-up places it in 2024, so timing is unresolved. SentinelOne says it was not compromised [S1][S4].

diamond.adversary: China-nexus cluster assessed by SentinelLABS with high confidence; loose ties to APT15 and UNC5174 [S2][S4].
diamond.capability: GoReShell Go-based reverse shell, THC tools, ShadowPad with ScatterBrain obfuscation [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: ORB network of relay boxes shared among several suspected Chinese actors [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Cybersecurity vendor and its logistics provider, a South Asian government-supporting entity, a European media organization [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing servers and gateway devices (Check Point gateways for the ShadowPad cluster) and third-party supply-chain providers [S2][S4].

gaps: I could not open the primary SentinelLABS report (WebFetch failed with a network error); all claims rely on search-result summaries and press coverage of it [S1].
Sponsor and objectives are not stated in the sources gathered; no government attribution found.
The APT15 and UNC5174 links are loose per SentinelLABS; the specific group behind PurpleHaze is unresolved [S2].

Initial access vector for PurpleHaze is unresolved. Check Point N-day exploitation is reported for the ShadowPad cluster [S2]; one advisory mentions Ivanti VPN, which was not confirmed in the sources I could read.

The ShadowPad cluster overlaps in public reporting with Orange Cyberdefense's Green Nailao activity (Check Point CVE-2024-24919, PlugX/ShadowPad, NailaoLocker ransomware); SentinelLABS did not confirm that mapping and the two should not be merged [S5].
Timing of the logistics provider breach differs across sources (2024 versus early 2025).
Individual victim names, post-exploitation objectives and data stolen are not public in sources gathered.
Existing encyclopedia text claiming possible ransomware deployment is not confirmed for PurpleHaze itself in my sources.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain includes internet-facing servers and gateway devices (VPN and firewall appliances) plus third-party suppliers such as hardware logistics providers [S1][S2][S4]. STEP 2: ORB networks make source attribution and blocking harder because infrastructure rotates among several suspected Chinese actors [S2][S3]. STEP 3: Observed pattern is reconnaissance of exposed servers over port 443, then GoReShell or ShadowPad with THC tooling for access [S2][S3][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued reconnaissance and intrusion against government, media and security-vendor targets and their suppliers. MDCOA is supply-chain access through a logistics or IT service provider into a defense-adjacent organization. Candidate indicators: repeated external connection attempts to exposed servers on 443, outbound SSH from servers, use of THC tools, and unexpected ShadowPad loader artifacts [S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor ORB and ShadowPad reporting and exposed-service reconnaissance logs; treat reconnaissance as possible precursor activity [S4]. (2) Authorities: third-party and contractor networks may sit outside direct DoD authority; coordinate through contract security and DC3 channels. (3) Mission assurance: inventory suppliers handling hardware and logistics, and exposed gateways, as mission-relevant cyber terrain [S1][S2]. (4) Coordination: because attribution among APT15, UNC5174 and APT41-associated clusters is unresolved, share indicators by cluster name and avoid merging vendor clusters [S1][S2].
